text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: preproc-service (us-west-2) p99 latency breached 5m ago. Streaming requests reporting tail stalls. Auto-page sent to oncall-eli.
oncall-eli: On it. Checking console and traces. Any customer-facing errors?
incident-bot: Errors observed: intermittent 504 on streaming endpoints, increased request duration spikes. Metrics: p95 ~ 1.2s -> 2.3s, p99 ~ 3.8s -> 12.5s last 10m. Tokenizer CPU and preproc CPU spiking.
sre-maya: Saw the same on infra dash. Node-level CPU on preproc pods at 95% for a subset. Rolling rest didn't help yet.
eng-runtime-omar: Taking a quick look at deploys — there was a rollout 25m ago: commit d4f9a7a added stricter prompt template validation for JSON-mode and a helper that runs a handful of regexes per tool schema.
ml-preproc-jen: That rings alarm bells — JSON-mode parsing runs a nested validator that can blow up on large tool schemas or deeply nested templates. We added some safety but maybe missed an input shape.
support-lee: Customers reporting long stalls and some timeouts: acct: acme-inc (prod), beta-app (eu-west), and 3 self-serve orgs. Support has open tickets with request IDs.
oncall-eli: Action plan idea: 1) Disable JSON-mode validation flag for streaming route immediately, 2) Route new requests to fallback model/variant, 3) Roll back commit if confirmed culprit. Any objections?
eng-runtime-omar: Agree. We can toggle the feature-flag via k8s config map and roll a fast restart. Also can route by policy to gpt-min latency model as fallback.
ml-preproc-jen: Quick mitigation: flip flag PREPROC_ENABLE_JSON_VALIDATION=false for the deployment in us-west-2 and restart pods. That will skip heavy schema checks and should reduce CPU. We should also increase preproc pod autoscaling temporarily.
sre-maya: I'll scale the HPA up (min replicas from 3 to 8) for preproc-usw2 now and monitor.
incident-bot: Runbook step triggered: page:ssr oncall, step: run-scaledown-unsuccessful if >15m.
support-lee: Please capture impacted customer list and any requests that got 504s so we can notify. I can correlate request IDs from logs.
eng-runtime-omar: Commands I'll run:```bash
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/preproc PREPROC_ENABLE_JSON_VALIDATION=false
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/preproc
```
ml-preproc-jen: Also temporary rule: if template_size > 12k chars, reject with 400 for streaming route until full fix. Adding a quick guard to upstream handler now.
oncall-eli: Doing handoff to sre-maya for infra actions, I'll stay for coordination with ML and Support. @sre-maya you're on primary.
sre-maya: Ack. Scaling HPA and restarting pods. Running:```bash
kubectl -n prod scale deployment/preproc --replicas=8
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/preproc
```
product-ana: We need to proactively notify affected customers. Support, compile list and I'll draft an email. Keep wording light: service degradation impacting streaming latency.
support-lee: Pulling request IDs: query:```sql
select org_id, request_id, status, ts from request_logs where service='preproc' and ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' and status in ('504','timeout');
```Will attach to ticket.
eng-runtime-omar: I also pushed a quick revert branch that removes the nested regex path for validators: PR #1428 (revert d4f9a7a). If mitigation isn't sufficient, we can deploy that as hotfix.
ml-preproc-jen: Root cause hypothesis: new prompt-template validation does a deep traversal with regex-based schema validation for JSON-mode. Certain user tool schemas trigger pathological cases leading to O(n*m) regex evals and catastrophic CPU. Streaming stalls are exacerbated because validation occurs on the hot path for each token stream start.
oncall-eli: Timeline: 00:00 alert, 00:02 paged, 00:05 mitigation flag flip started, 00:08 HPA scaled, 00:12 pods restarted, 00:18 p99 dropping but not back to baseline.
sre-maya: After restarts, p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 4.0s — improved but still high. Some pods still warm up due to large caches and KV warming.
eng-runtime-omar: I'll route new streaming requests to fallback model variant (lower-latency) for 20m to reduce customer impact: updating routing policy now.
product-ana: Can we confirm which SLAs are affected? Support, list customers with paid SLAs so we prioritize outreach.
support-lee: Confirmed: acme-inc and beta-app on paid tiers. Notifying both now, including ask to retry and apologies.
ml-preproc-jen: For a durable fix: 1) Replace regex-heavy schema validator with a streaming-safe parser (switch to jsonschema-lite), 2) Add template size checks and compile-time caching, 3) Offload heavy validation to asynchronous job for non-streaming requests. I'll open tasks and PRs.
oncall-eli: Any risk to data correctness if we disable validation? We need to ensure we don't silently accept invalid tool-schema that breaks downstream.
ml-preproc-jen: Short-term tradeoff: skipping deep validation for streaming only; we still do basic syntactic checks and enforce a blacklist for obviously malformed inputs. Downstream services have guards too. We'll capture failures and escalate if they appear.
sre-maya: Monitoring: enabling additional traces for preproc/validation path and adding alerts for error-rate spike if it increases after flag flip.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Escalation: eng-runtime-omar and ml-preproc-jen assigned.
eng-runtime-omar: Deploying revert PR now if needed. If p99 doesn't stabilize to <2s in 30m, we'll deploy revert.
product-ana: Please add estimated customer impact numbers to postmortem: % of requests affected, durations, and root-cause summary.
support-lee: Noted. I'll attach the query results and top customer request traces.
ml-preproc-jen: Started implementing quick guard commit: limit template_size, avoid heavy regex for nested objects. Pushing branch preproc-hotfix-1428.
oncall-eli: Handoff update: I'm dropping to watch mode — @sre-maya you own infra, @eng-runtime-omar & @ml-preproc-jen own code fix. I'll coordinate external comms.
sre-maya: Green check — after additional autoscaling and warmed caches, p99 steady ~1.9s over last 5m. No new 504 spikes.
incident-bot: Incident update: p99 back under alert threshold for 10m. Auto-close scheduled in 30m unless reopened.
product-ana: Good. Start postmortem draft and include customer notification drafts.
support-lee: I'll follow up with acme-inc and beta-app with incident summary and mitigation steps.
eng-runtime-omar: I'll prepare the revert PR ready to go, but won't deploy since metrics look stable. We'll schedule a patch to replace validator and add caching.
ml-preproc-jen: Opening follow-ups: TICKET-3142 (replace validator), TICKET-3143 (compile-time caching), TICKET-3144 (async validation pipeline).
oncall-eli: Thanks everyone. If anything flips, re-page. Closing handoff to SRE; I'm available for comms.
product-ana: Nice work triaging quickly. We'll review postmortem with customers.
sre-maya: Marking incident as resolved from infra side.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: preproc-service latency spike mitigated. Duration: ~00:40. Participants: oncall-eli, sre-maya, eng-runtime-omar, ml-preproc-jen, support-lee, product-ana. Postmortem link to follow. :white_check_mark:
